claims.text: R-Dub QuickLog is designed to track the product used, dose, method of use, intended purpose, effects, and changes across repeated experiences over time.
limitations: This is project methodology from the public Real Data Project page, not an efficacy finding.
claims.citation_locator: Real World Data Exchange (R-Dub) Platform > QuickLog Your Experiences

claims.text: The MoreBetter Functional Beverage Study public page reports 4,873 verified participants, 58,000+ logged use sessions, 39 products, and 26 brands over a 22-day study period.
limitations: Counts are taken from the project company's public study page; the underlying participant-level dataset is not stored here.
claims.citation_locator: Functional Beverage Study public landing page

claims.text: Science of Smokability Phase I compared cannabis flower at 0.45, 0.65, and 0.85 water activity and evaluated chemical composition together with smoking-quality or sensory measures.
limitations: The study is a controlled post-harvest experiment, not a clinical trial.
claims.citation_locator: Study introduction/method description and Phase I project page

claims.text: The Phase I report states that 0.65 aW flower produced the highest terpene content, 0.85 aW reduced measured cannabinoid levels, and sensory panelists reported more irritation with the drier 0.45 aW condition.
limitations: Results apply to the study materials and conditions; they should not be treated as a universal curing target without replication across cultivars and processes.
claims.citation_locator: Cannabis Science and Technology 2025;8(2):10-19 key results

claims.text: The public Science of Smokability Phase II page describes a planned study of nutrients and flushing; this registry does not treat the project page itself as evidence of an outcome.
limitations: Protocol/project metadata only; outcome claims require a verified results publication.
claims.citation_locator: Science of Smokability Phase II project page

claims.text: The 2026 CHS survey included 1,134 participants in its final analysis and collected anonymous self-reported cannabis-consumption patterns and CHS-related symptoms from respondents recruited through CHS-focused online communities.
limitations: The self-selected, self-reported survey design limits generalizability and does not establish causation.
claims.citation_locator: PubMed abstract Materials and methods / Results

claims.text: In the CHS survey sample, 96.5% reported using cannabis at least daily around the relevant period, and 45% reported using it six or more times per day around symptom development.
limitations: These percentages describe a CHS-focused convenience sample and must not be interpreted as risk estimates for cannabis users generally.

claims.text: The 2026 Mitragyna speciosa study used a 7-day baseline followed by 14 days of daily observational reporting, with self-selected and self-reported dose and repeated structured questionnaires; this is a reusable longitudinal RWE method pattern, not cannabis efficacy evidence.
limitations: The study organism/product is kratom, not cannabis; only the longitudinal methodology is transferable.
claims.citation_locator: Frontiers in Pharmacology Methods, participant reporting design
